Zoho Recruit pricing starts at $0/month on the Forever Free plan and scales to $75/user/month on the Staffing Agency Enterprise tier, billed annually. With just one active job slot and no resume parsing, AI features, or sourcing tools, it's functional only for a solo recruiter filling a single position at a time.

An ATS and recruiting CRM used primarily by small-to-midsize teams and staffing agencies, Zoho Recruit earns a 4.5/5 on [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/125768/Zoho-Recruit/reviews/) from 1,147 reviews (January 2026). Users praise its price-to-feature ratio and Zoho ecosystem integrations. But the platform has a quirk most buyers don't realize. It ships as two separate editions, Corporate HR and Staffing Agency, each with different plan structures, job limits, and feature sets at the same price point.

This Zoho Recruit pricing 2026 breakdown covers every plan across both editions and the add-on costs that inflate your bill. It evaluates whether the free tier is genuinely usable and how five alternatives compare.

> **TL;DR:**
>
> - **Forever Free is usable only for solo recruiters with one opening.** 1 active job, no resume parsing, no AI, 5 email templates. You outgrow it in a week.
> - **Two editions at the same price, 10x different limits.** Corporate HR Standard caps at 10 active jobs; Staffing Agency Standard gets 100 at the same $25/user/mo rate.
> - **AI shows up at Professional ($50/user/mo).** Zia candidate matching, AI assessments, SMS, and phone integration are gated behind the Pro tier.
> - **Per-user pricing doesn't scale.** At 5+ users, flat-rate platforms beat Zoho's per-seat model. Add-ons and agentic AI features push real costs 30-50% above sticker.
> - **No built-in candidate database.** Zoho is an ATS, not a sourcing tool. For proactive outreach across 850M+ profiles, pair it with (or replace it with) [Pin](https://www.pin.com/) at $100/mo.

## What Are Zoho Recruit Pricing Plans in 2026?

_Prices verified against_ [_Zoho's official pricing page_](https://www.zoho.com/recruit/pricing.html) _as of March 2026._

Four tiers span Zoho Recruit's pricing page from $0 to $75/user/month, but the actual cost depends on which edition you pick. Staffing Agency includes three paid tiers while Corporate HR has only two. Both share the same free plan.

One detail trips up most buyers: the Corporate HR edition has no Professional tier. You go straight from Standard ($25/user/month, 10 active jobs) to Enterprise ($50/user/month, 20 active jobs). By contrast, Staffing Agency offers Standard (100 jobs), Professional (250 jobs), and Enterprise (750 jobs). Same price, wildly different limits.

### Staffing Agency Edition Pricing

| Plan | Monthly Cost (Annual Billing) | Active Jobs | Resume Parsing | AI Features |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Forever Free | $0 | 1 | None | None |
| Standard | $25/user/month | 100 | 250/day | None |
| Professional | $50/user/month | 250 | 500/day | Zia Matching, AI Assessments |
| Enterprise | $75/user/month | 750 | Unlimited | Full suite + client portals |

### Corporate HR Edition Pricing

| Plan | Monthly Cost (Annual Billing) | Active Jobs | Resume Parsing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Forever Free | $0 | 1 | None |
| Standard | $25/user/month | 10 | 250/day |
| Enterprise | $50/user/month | 20 | Unlimited |

Most buyers overlook Zoho Recruit's two-edition split entirely. A staffing agency paying $25/user/month on Standard gets 100 active jobs. A corporate HR team paying that same $25/user/month on Standard gets 10. That's a 10x difference for the same money. In-house recruiters managing more than 10 openings will hit the cap quickly, and the only upgrade path doubles the cost to $50/user/month for just 20 jobs.

**What we're seeing:** Most teams evaluating Zoho Recruit land on it for one reason - they're already inside the Zoho ecosystem. Outside that context, the decision usually comes down to team size and whether proactive sourcing is on the agenda. In the Pin 2026 user survey, 91% of users said they reduced or eliminated LinkedIn Recruiter spend after switching to Pin. Overall recruiting spend dropped 90% across tools, job boards, and agency fees combined. That pattern matters when evaluating an ATS like Zoho Recruit as a cost-cutting move. Tracking applicants already in your pipeline is where Zoho excels. Finding candidates who haven't applied yet is a different problem - an ATS adds overhead rather than capacity. Recognizing which problem you actually have before buying is the most important step in any ATS evaluation.

## What's Included in Each Plan?

Paid tiers unlock dramatically more than the free plan. Eight agentic AI tools launched in October 2025 - including a Sourcing Bot, Screening Bot, and AI-powered candidate assessments - ship bundled into paid plans at no extra charge, according to [Small Biz Trends](https://smallbiztrends.com/zoho-recruit-brings-agentic-ai-tools-to-streamline-hiring-and-collaboration/) (October 2025). Zoho Recruit pricing for AI features starts at the Professional tier ($50/user/month), with nothing on Standard or Free.

| Feature | Free | Standard ($25) | Professional ($50) | Enterprise ($75) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Resume Parsing | - | 250/day | 500/day | Unlimited |
| Email Templates | 5 | 100 | 250 | Unlimited |
| Custom Fields | - | 50 | 150 | 300 |
| Social Recruiting | - | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Google for Jobs | - | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| AI Candidate Matching | - | - | ✅ (Zia) | ✅ (Zia) |
| AI Assessments | - | - | ✅ | ✅ |
| SMS / Phonebridge | - | - | ✅ | ✅ |
| Client Portal | - | - | - | ✅ (or add-on) |
| Workflow Automation | - | Basic | Advanced | Advanced + territory mgmt |
| Analytics / Dashboards | - | Standard | Advanced | Advanced + custom |
| Integrations (50+) | - | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Support | 8/5 | 8/5 | 8/5 | Priority |

At the Professional tier, Zoho Recruit becomes a genuinely competitive ATS. You get AI candidate matching through Zia, SMS outreach, phone integration, and 500 resume parses per day. Below that, Standard is a functional tracking system with no AI and limited automation. It gets the job done for teams that mostly need to organize applications they already receive.

One notable gap across all tiers: Zoho Recruit doesn't include a large candidate database for proactive sourcing. It's an applicant tracking system first. If you need to search millions of profiles and run automated outreach sequences, you'll need a separate sourcing tool alongside it. Pin, for example, includes an 850M+ candidate database with AI sourcing and multi-channel outreach starting at $100/month - a different category than what Zoho Recruit offers.

## Is Zoho Recruit's Free Plan Worth It?

For most teams, no. Zoho Recruit's Forever Free plan supports exactly one active job at a time with 256MB of storage, five email templates, and zero resume parsing, according to [Zoho's plan comparison page](https://www.zoho.com/recruit/plan-comparison.html) (2026). Zoho Recruit free plan limitations are deliberately extensive: no AI tools, no resume parsing, no job board posting, and no integrations. Zoho's free tier functions as an onboarding gateway rather than a production-ready recruiting tool.

Zoho's free tier includes just the bare minimum for candidate tracking:

-   **1 active job** per recruiter license at a time
-   **Candidate management** - basic profile storage and tracking
-   **Email management** - send from the platform, but limited to 5 templates
-   **Interview scheduling** - calendar coordination built in
-   **256MB storage** - enough for a few hundred candidate records
-   **8/5 support** - business hours only, no weekend coverage

Missing features on the free plan:

-   **No resume parsing** - you manually enter every candidate detail
-   **No sourcing tools** - no Source Boosters, no social recruiting
-   **No custom fields** - you can't adapt the platform to your workflow
-   **No reporting or dashboards** - no analytics of any kind
-   **No AI features** - none of the Zia-powered tools available on paid plans
-   **No integrations** - can't connect to your existing stack

Who should actually use it? A solo recruiter filling one contract role or a very early-stage startup with a single open position. That's it. Once you need two concurrent job postings, the free tier stops working. Evaluating Zoho Recruit's free plan as a long-term solution for a team of any size means looking at the wrong product - you'll outgrow it within a week.

By comparison, platforms like Breezy HR also offer a free tier with one active job but include a branded career site and basic pipeline management. Neither free tier replaces a paid tool for active recruiting.

### Free Tier Verdict by Team Type

A quick pass/fail assessment of Zoho Recruit free plan details by use case:

| Team Type | Free Tier Viable? | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solo recruiter, 1 open role | ✅ Viable | The 1-job limit works. Basic candidate tracking is functional. |
| Startup with 2-3 openings | ❌ Not viable | Can't manage multiple jobs simultaneously. Upgrade required immediately. |
| Small agency | ❌ Not viable | No client portal, no resume parsing, no sourcing. Missing core agency features. |
| In-house HR team | ❌ Not viable | No custom fields, no reporting, no integrations with HRIS systems. |
| Enterprise | ❌ Not viable | No compliance features, no advanced security, no analytics. |

Primarily an onboarding ramp, the free plan exists to get recruiters into the Zoho ecosystem - with the expectation that they'll upgrade once they see the interface and commit to the workflow. It's a product demo disguised as a plan tier. That's not inherently dishonest, but it means you shouldn't evaluate Zoho Recruit's value based on what the free tier offers. Real functionality starts at $25/user/month.

## What Are the Hidden Costs?

Advertised per-user pricing is rarely what teams actually pay for Zoho Recruit. Based on [Zoho's published add-on rates](https://www.zoho.com/recruit/pricing.html) (2026), modules like client portals, video interviews, and storage upgrades can push the real monthly cost 30-50% above the base rate. Those extras carry a real price:

| Add-On | Monthly Cost | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client Portal | $6/license/month | Required for staffing agencies sharing candidate pools with clients |
| Video Interviews | $12/license/month | Per-job-opening pricing also available |
| Extra Storage (5GB) | $4.60/month | Base storage fills fast with resumes and attachments |
| Data Backup | $11.50/month | Automated backup of your recruiting data |
| Vendor Portal | Billed annually | For agencies managing external vendors |

A realistic monthly bill for a 3-person recruiting team on Standard breaks down like this:

A 3-person team that expected to pay $75/month is actually paying $109.60 - a 46% increase. A 5-person Professional team with the same add-ons faces a steeper bill: $250 base + $30 client portal + $12 video + $4.60 storage = $296.60/month, or $3,559/year.

Expensive or not depends on the comparison. As a standalone ATS, Zoho Recruit's total cost still undercuts enterprise platforms like iCIMS or Workday by a wide margin. But flat-rate competitors like [JazzHR](/blog/jazzhr-pricing/) ($75/month for up to 3 active jobs) and Breezy HR ($157/month for unlimited users) don't charge per seat, which makes them more predictable as your team grows.

## How Does Zoho Recruit's Per-User Cost Scale?

Per-user pricing works well for Zoho Recruit teams of one to three. Past that, the math starts favoring flat-rate alternatives. A 5-person team on Zoho Professional pays $3,000/year in base fees alone - before add-ons - while flat-rate tools like Breezy HR Startup charge $1,884/year regardless of team size.

<figure style="margin:2rem 0;padding:0;line-height:0"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Annual Cost for a 5-Person Team (Base Price)" style="width:100%;height:auto;display:block;border-radius:12px"></figure>

At 10 users, the gap widens further. Zoho Professional hits $6,000/year while JazzHR stays at $900 and Breezy remains at $1,884. This doesn't mean Zoho is overpriced - it means the per-user model has a breakeven point, and past it, you're paying for scaling that flat-rate tools absorb into a fixed fee.

Cheap or expensive isn't the right question for Zoho Recruit. What matters is whether per-user pricing fits your team size and growth trajectory. A solo recruiter or team of two will find Zoho's model hard to beat. A 10-person agency is likely better off with a flat-rate ATS or a sourcing-first platform that bundles more capability per dollar.

## What Changed in Zoho Recruit for 2025-2026?

Eight agentic AI tools and a full telephony integration represent the most aggressive Zoho Recruit update cycle in its history, landing across late 2025 and early 2026, according to [Zoho's 2025 Year in Review](https://www.zoho.com/blog/recruit/year-in-review-2025-zoho-recruit.html). What's new matters for pricing decisions because the value gap between Standard and Professional widened significantly.

### AI Features (October 2025)

October 2025 brought a Sourcing Bot, Screening Bot, AI-powered candidate matching through Zia, and AI Assessments that generate role-specific evaluation questions. All ship with paid plans at no additional cost. That's a meaningful difference from competitors that charge separate AI add-on fees or gate AI behind their highest tiers.

One catch: these AI features only work with candidates already in your Zoho Recruit database. Its Sourcing Bot searches your existing pool - it doesn't tap into an external database. Teams with thousands of archived candidates will find this useful. Teams starting fresh have nothing for the AI to work with until they've built a pipeline through other channels.

### 2026 Updates

Early 2026 brought built-in telephony (no external PBX system required), job alerts for candidates, auto-trigger capabilities for the Screening Bot, and shared record ownership for team collaboration. Built-in telephony eliminates the previous dependency on Zoho Phonebridge or third-party phone integrations - one less add-on to budget for on higher-tier plans.

A Blocked Candidates feature added in January 2026 lets recruiters flag candidates they don't want surfaced in future searches. Small feature, but it signals that Zoho is investing in workflow refinements alongside the big AI releases.

Bottom line for pricing: the AI additions make Zoho's Professional plan ($50/user/month) significantly more competitive than it was a year ago. AI candidate matching, automated screening, and AI assessments are now bundled into a price point that hasn't changed. Anyone who evaluated Zoho Recruit in 2024 and passed should take a second look at the 2025-2026 feature set.

Each alternative trades something for something else. Manatal is the cheapest per-user option at $15/month, but lacks a free tier and doesn't include workflow automation until higher plans. JazzHR gives you predictable flat-rate pricing, but caps active jobs at 3 on the entry tier. Workable delivers the most polished interface and includes built-in sourcing, but $299/month is a jump for teams used to $25-$50 per seat. Where does Zoho Recruit fit? Zoho Recruit is strongest for teams already inside the Zoho ecosystem. Running Zoho CRM, Zoho Books, or Zoho People means the 45+ native integrations create a unified workflow without third-party middleware.

Outside that ecosystem, the value proposition weakens. Dated interface feedback appears consistently in user reviews on [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/125768/Zoho-Recruit/reviews/) (4.5/5, 1,147 reviews) and [G2](https://www.g2.com/products/zoho-recruit/reviews/) (4.4/5, 2026), and per-user cost scaling hurts competitiveness as teams grow.

Applicant tracking and pipeline management is where Zoho Recruit earns its place as a solid mid-tier option. Proactive candidate sourcing - searching databases, running multi-channel outreach, and automating interview scheduling - is a different category entirely, and Zoho Recruit doesn't play in it at any price tier. For that use case, Pin is the best sourcing platform for recruiters who need to go outbound. Rated 4.8/5 on G2, Pin searches 850M+ profiles with automated multi-channel outreach that reduces time-to-hire by 82%.

As Rich Rosen, Executive Recruiter at Cornerstone Search, puts it: "Absolutely money maker for recruiters... in 6 months I can directly attribute over $250K in revenue to Pin." That kind of ROI comes from sourcing and outreach capabilities - the exact features Zoho Recruit lacks regardless of which plan you're on.

## When Does Zoho Recruit Make Sense?

Zoho Recruit makes the most sense for solo recruiters, small teams of 2-3, and companies already running the Zoho ecosystem. Past 5 users, the per-user cost model starts losing to flat-rate alternatives. A quick breakdown by use case:

### Good Fit

-   **Solo recruiters or 2-person teams** who need a basic ATS and are comfortable with Zoho's interface. The Standard plan at $25-$50/month total is competitive.
-   **Zoho ecosystem users** who already run Zoho CRM, Zoho People, or Zoho Books. The native integrations save time and eliminate data silos.
-   **Staffing agencies managing 100+ active jobs** on the Staffing Standard tier. The $25/user/month price for 100 job slots is reasonable for agencies with volume.
-   **Budget-conscious teams** that need ATS functionality without enterprise pricing. Even with add-ons, Zoho Recruit stays well below iCIMS or Workday territory.

### Not a Good Fit

-   **Growing teams of 5+ recruiters** where per-user costs compound quickly. Flat-rate alternatives save money at scale.
-   **Corporate HR teams needing more than 20 active jobs** - the Corporate Enterprise cap is restrictive, and there's no higher tier.
-   **Teams that need proactive sourcing** - Zoho Recruit tracks applicants, it doesn't find them. You'll need a separate sourcing tool.
-   **Anyone expecting a modern UI** - the interface consistently gets called "dated" and "cluttered" in user reviews on [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/125768/Zoho-Recruit/reviews/) (2026).

When sourcing is the bottleneck rather than tracking, consider whether an [ATS alone is what you need](https://www.pin.com/blog/ats-vs-crm-recruiters/) or whether a platform that combines AI sourcing, automated outreach, and scheduling would deliver better [recruiting ROI](https://www.pin.com/blog/recruiting-roi-ai-tools/).

### Which Zoho Recruit Plan Should You Pick?

Committed to Zoho Recruit? Here is a decision framework based on what we've covered:

1.  **Free:** Testing the platform for a single role. Don't commit budget until you've confirmed the interface works. Expect to upgrade within days if you're actively hiring.
2.  **Standard ($25/user/month):** Small teams that need a functional ATS with resume parsing, social recruiting, and basic automation. Good enough for organizing inbound applications.
3.  **Professional ($50/user/month):** The sweet spot for AI candidate matching, SMS outreach, and advanced analytics. Best value for teams of 1-3 recruiters.
4.  **Enterprise ($75/user/month):** Staffing agencies managing high volume with client portals, territory management, and field-level security. Only justified if you need client-facing features or the 750-job cap.

Before committing, calculate your total cost including likely add-ons. Per-user rates are the floor, not the ceiling, once you factor in add-ons. A team of 5+ recruiters should run the math against flat-rate alternatives before signing a contract.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much does Zoho Recruit cost per month?

Zoho Recruit pricing starts at $0/month on the Forever Free plan and scales to $75/user/month on the Staffing Agency Enterprise tier, billed annually. Standard ($25/user/month) and Professional ($50/user/month) are the two most popular paid tiers. For a 3-person team on Standard, the base monthly cost is $75 - but add-ons like client portal, video interviews, and extra storage typically push the real total to $109-$120/month. Annual billing is required to get these rates; month-to-month billing is not available by default.

### Is Zoho Recruit free?

Yes, Zoho Recruit has a free plan with no expiration date, but it's limited to one active job at a time. It includes no resume parsing, no AI tools, and no integrations. Functional for a solo recruiter testing the platform; any team with two or more concurrent openings will need the $25/user/month Standard plan within days.

### What is the Zoho Recruit forever free plan?

Zoho Recruit's Forever Free plan allows one active job at a time, 256MB of storage, and five email templates. It includes no resume parsing, no AI features, no social recruiting, and no integrations with other tools. The plan is functional for a solo recruiter testing the platform or filling a single position. Any team managing more than one open role simultaneously will need to upgrade to the Standard plan at $25/user/month.

### What is the alternative to Zoho Recruit?

Choosing the right alternative depends on what you need. For a low-cost ATS with per-user pricing, [Manatal](/blog/manatal-pricing/) ($15/user/month) is the cheapest option. For flat-rate billing that scales without compounding seat costs, JazzHR ($75/month) and Breezy HR ($157/month) are solid choices. For teams that need proactive candidate sourcing alongside applicant tracking, Pin is the best alternative to Zoho Recruit. Rated 4.8/5 on G2, Pin's flat-rate plans start at $100/month and include AI search across 850M+ profiles, automated outreach, and interview scheduling. Many teams pair Zoho Recruit for ATS with Pin for sourcing and outreach to cover the full top-of-funnel workflow.

### Does Zoho Recruit include AI features?

Yes, but only on paid plans. Zoho added eight AI-powered features in October 2025, including a Sourcing Bot, Screening Bot, and AI candidate matching through its Zia engine. These are included at no extra cost on Professional ($50/user/month) and Enterprise ($75/user/month) tiers. The Standard and Free plans don't include any AI tools.

### What's the difference between Zoho Recruit's Corporate and Staffing editions?

Corporate HR supports fewer active jobs (10-20 per plan) with just two paid tiers (Standard and Enterprise). Staffing Agency covers 100-750 active jobs and adds a Professional tier with AI candidate matching. Both editions cost the same per user, but agencies get significantly more capacity for their money.

### Can Zoho Recruit replace a dedicated sourcing tool?

No. Zoho Recruit is an applicant tracking system that manages candidates who've already applied or been manually added. It doesn't include a candidate database for proactive outreach. Platforms like [Pin's AI sourcing](https://www.pin.com/), which searches 850M+ profiles and automates multi-channel outreach with 5x better response rates than industry averages, serve a fundamentally different function. Many teams run both an ATS and a sourcing tool.
